newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada March wholesale trade falls from February.
newsitem.headline: Canada March wholesale trade falls from February.

text.p: Canada's wholesale trade fell 2.7 percent on a seasonally adjusted basis in March from February to C$22.46 billion, Statistics Canada said on Tuesday.
Sales, adj C$22.46 bln -2.7 pct +8.1 pct
Inventories, adj C$32.89 bln -0.1 pct +3.6 pct
Note - dollar figures are billions. Other figures are percentage changes.
A Reuters survey of economists had forecast a 1.2 percent month-on-month rise in March.
StatsCan also revised its figure for February sales to C$23.08 billion from C$23.09 billion.
The federal agency said most sectors recorded lower sales in March compared with February, with the exception of the other products category, which rose 1.5 percent, and food, which rose 0.3 percent.

The agency said the two largest declines in March occurred in the same sectors that reported the largest increases in February. Sales of wholesale farm machinery and equipment dropped 14.2 percent in March, following a 16.3 percent jump in February. Motor vehicles and parts fell 11.1 percent after advancing 8.9 percent a month earlier.
Sales of computers and packaged software fell 6.6 percent in March after three months of strong increases, Statistics Canada said.

Sales by wholesalers in the first quarter of 1997 were 11 percent higher than the same quarter a year earlier, the agency said. First quarter sales were especially strong for lumber and building materials wholesalers, up 23.9 percent.

Inventories in March moved only slightly, down 0.1 percent to C$32.8 billion, after seven months of increases. The inventory-to-sales ratio increased to 1.46 in March from 1.43 February, the lowest level since December 1994.
